title: Stretch for five minutes: a gentle start anywhere
description: No mat, no kit, no floor work. Five standing stretches, one minute each, to unkink a body that has been sitting too long — at home, at work, anywhere.

body.heading: Why five minutes works
paragraphs: Long sitting leaves the neck, shoulders, back and hips quietly tightening, and the fix does not require a workout — it requires interruption. A few gentle stretches restore range of motion, wake up circulation, and give your eyes and mind a genuine break from the screen.
Set a timer for five minutes. Every stretch below is done standing, holding on to a chair or wall whenever balance feels uncertain.

body.heading: The five stretches
paragraphs: One: neck — drop your right ear slowly towards your right shoulder, hold for a slow count of ten, then swap sides. Two: shoulders — roll both shoulders in big slow circles, five forwards, five back. Three: chest — clasp your hands behind your back and lift them gently as you open your chest.

Four: side bend — one hand on the chair, the other arm reaching up and over, ten slow seconds each side. Five: calves — hands on the wall, one foot stepped back with the heel pressed down, ten seconds each leg. Breathe normally throughout; a stretch should feel like a pull, never like pain.

body.heading: Make it a habit, not an event
paragraphs: Attach the five minutes to something that already happens: the kettle boiling, a call ending, the top of the hour. Habits that ride on existing moments survive; habits that need their own ceremony rarely do.

If any movement hurts sharply, or you have an injury, a recent operation or a condition that affects movement, skip that stretch and ask a doctor or physiotherapist what suits your body. Gentle is the whole point.

takeaway: Five standing stretches, one minute each, attached to a moment that already happens — gentle movement, never pain.
materials: A chair or wall for balance
Comfortable shoes or bare feet on a non-slip floor
supervision: Independent activity for adults; children copy a grown-up and keep every movement gentle.
safetyNotes: Stop any stretch that causes sharp pain, dizziness or numbness.
Hold furniture for balance whenever you feel unsteady, and keep the floor around you clear.
If you have an injury, recent surgery or a health condition affecting movement, check with a doctor or physiotherapist before stretching.
